# ACL config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/acl/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.ACLBlock` and, after composition onto the kernel Root, drives the unchanged ADR-010 ACL engine. A singleton kind: one `acl` block with a default action and an ordered rule list; a second file is a merge conflict. RBAC roles/bindings (the golden path) compile down to this vocabulary — hand-authoring `acl` is the escape hatch.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `config/acl` |
| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `singleton` — the kind itself is the identity; neither the stem nor a label carries meaning (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `acl` |
| Loader directory | `.tera/acl/<name>.hcl` |
| Go source | `github.com/kottera/kottera/pkg/config.ACLBlock` |
| Served at | `GET /api/v1/schemas/config/acl/reference` |

## Example

A minimal `acl`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/acl/example-acl.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

acl {
  rule "example" {
    principal = "worker:example-worker"
    action    = "invoke"
    resource  = "api/v1/workorders/list"
    effect    = "allow"
  }
}
```
